optimization: coalesce final file data syncs per replicated application and use the existing executor with a two-worker bound
method: OrbStack Linux native data volume, 8 CPUs, 8 GiB, GOMAXPROCS=2 per replica; 1002 entities, 4 writers and 16 readers, 20 host/service groups per batch; Require every replica to finish seed index rebuild before restart; 5s read warmup, 30s measurement plus request tail. Sample resources only after every replica applies the leader committed position; publication throughput elapsed excludes the extra replica drain; before1/after/before2 with order reversed in round 2. Same host has unrelated workloads.
application_metric_contract: Successful applied log entries and application transactions, summed across replicas, sampled sequentially before and after each load. Includes control and empty entries. Counters reset on restart. Both revisions expose these counters.
exploration_reason: Exploratory windows lacked per-replica seed index readiness and application drain checks. Some replicas checkpointed a translated cancellation at shutdown, skipping index rebuild. None of these windows is used for final performance attribution.
readiness_contract: Each replica must record seed index_rebuild_completed before profiling restart. Before and after load, all replicas must reach the leader committed index and expose no application or snapshot error. All replicas are full voters.

historical_log_audit.scope: Retrospective event presence check only, not equivalent to the new pre-restart gate or post-load application drain.

local_benchmark.method: Existing BenchmarkReplicatedFilePublication, 16 objects of 1 KiB, twice per application; OrbStack Linux native data volume, 4 CPUs, 6 GiB, GOMAXPROCS=2, 10 iterations per sample, 3 samples in each before1/after/before2 block. Sync counts include FileStore file and directory barriers, excluding bbolt syncs.

reused_update_content.reason: The temporary reopen harness reused the update epoch check on the same data. Twenty updates were correctly logical_noop, so 43 successful requests produced 23 graph versions. Corrected to a different data update epoch for each revision before rerunning all eight combinations.
